mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 engine typically costs between £6,500 and £9,500 for supply only. Reconditioned units start around £5,000, while used engines can be found from £2,800. Prices vary based on whether you choose supply-only or a full supply and fit service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil pump failure in a Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include a distinct metallic knocking or rumbling noise from the bottom of the engine, particularly during cold starts. You might also experience fluctuating oil pressure warnings on the dashboard or metallic flakes in the engine oil.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for well-maintained, higher-value examples. A Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 in good condition holds a value of £4,000 to £14,000+. Investing £5,000-£7,500 in a reconditioned engine with a 12-month warranty is financially viable if you plan to keep the vehicle long-term, though lower-value examples may warrant a used engine or part-exchange evaluation.

mainEntity.name: What is the 276DT engine code in the Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 276DT is the specific 2.7-litre V6 turbodiesel engine code fitted to the first-generation L320 Range Rover Sport (2005-2010). It is a Ford/PSA Lion V6 unit, sharing its architecture with the Discovery 3, and is known for strong towing torque but specific oil pump housing weaknesses.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 typically takes 2 to 3 working days. This includes the removal of the old unit, thorough cleaning of the engine bay, installation of the replacement engine, and comprehensive system testing.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched in 2005, the Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 brought robust V6 diesel power to the first-generation L320 model, sharing its Ford/PSA Lion V6 architecture with the Discovery 3 to deliver strong towing capability and motorway refinement.

milestones.description: 276DT engine code introduced, 2.7L, 190hp (Replaced the V8 petrol as the volume seller for the new L320 platform, offering 440Nm of torque but introducing known oil pump and crankshaft vulnerabilities).
2.7 TDV6 phased out in favour of the 3.0 TDV6 (306DT) for the L320 facelift, though many 2.7 TDV6 models remained in active service across the UK.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: Oil Pump & Crankshaft Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 2.7 TDV6 276DT Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The oil pump housing has a known weak point at the tensioner mount. Failure leads to sudden oil starvation, bearing spin, and catastrophic crankshaft fracture, often without prior warning.
